rv.q: The production, directed by Esteban Andres Cruz, is harrowingly intimate and a fantastic example of what is possible in theatre at any scale.
With City Lit’s production drawing clear parallels to today’s headlines, especially through projections designed by Andres Fiz, this 25-year-old play feels disturbingly relevant.
Stephen Adly Guirgis’ “Jesus Hopped the ‘A’ Train,” beautifully mounted by City Lit, shows us what live theater can be.

Notable New York playwright Stephen Adly Guirgis’s 2000 breakthrough play, “Jesus Hopped the 'A' Train,” is receiving a dynamic revival at City Lit Theater, with a fantastic cast delivering excellent performances and inventive staging, all under the direction of Esteban Andres Cruz.

Cruz's sure-handed and imaginative production gives all the actors in the ensemble a chance to shine, and it's a particular triumph for Izquierdo and Stevens, who make every moment of their jailhouse encounters count.
This is one of the most thought-provoking productions of the year thus far.
It is an amazing production, and you should see it now!

cn.t: City Lit's revival of Guirgis's raw 2000 drama earns strong praise for its harrowing intimacy, inventive staging, and powerful performances—one outlier finds it uneven, but critics largely call it essential theater.
